title: The Gingerbread Man
description: Fresh from the oven, one very fast cookie leads the whole countryside on a merry chase. A playful retelling of the classic runaway-cookie tale.

pages.alt: A grandmother in a cozy kitchen opens the oven, where a gingerbread man cookie glows warm.
pages.text: One afternoon, a grandmother baked a gingerbread man with icing hair and two red candy buttons. But when the oven door opened — pop! — out he jumped, right onto his cookie feet.

pages.alt: The gingerbread man runs down a garden path while the grandmother chases behind.
pages.text: “Stop, little cookie!” called the grandmother. But he only ran faster, singing, “Run, run, as fast as you can — you can't catch me, I'm the gingerbread man!”

pages.alt: A big brown bear watches the gingerbread man dash across a green meadow.
pages.text: He raced past a bear with a rumbling tummy. “Halt, little snack!” said the bear. But the gingerbread man just laughed and sang his song, and the bear was left far behind.

pages.alt: A white goat looks up as the gingerbread man runs by in the sunshine.
pages.text: He zipped past a goat chewing daisies. “Baa! Come back!” bleated the goat. But nobody — nobody! — was as fast as the gingerbread man.

pages.alt: The gingerbread man stops at a wide blue river, where an orange fox waits nearby.
pages.text: Then he came to a wide, wet river. Cookies cannot swim! “Hop onto my back,” said a smooth voice. It was a fox, smiling a foxy smile. “I'll carry you across.”

pages.alt: The fox swims across the river with the gingerbread man balanced on his nose.
pages.text: Into the water they went. “The river is deep — climb up to my nose!” said the fox. The gingerbread man climbed higher and higher… and SNAP! The clever fox gobbled him up, every last crumb.

pages.alt: Back home at night, the grandmother sets a fresh tray of gingerbread by the window.
pages.text: Back home, the grandmother smiled and mixed another bowl of dough. “This time,” she said, “I'll bake the buttons on tight — and eat my cookies warm.” And that is just what she did.
